turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about that zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; who decided that?
Don't manage me. I asked you something specific. Was Owen heard before that mark went in, yes or no?
But I'm not changing the grade.

That isn't an answer, it's a decision you made before you'd spoken to anyone. Your own procedure, 4.2, says I get a call before any mark is entered, and I didn't get one. On what basis is that zero staying, or do I walk upstairs to the principal right now?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"Keep going if you like." I'm writing that down, along with the fact that you still haven't told me what that zero rests on. Either you show me something with a date on it, or my next stop is the principal's office and then the board.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

Then I'll want that no in an email, Hale, with whatever you think it stands on. And tell me now whether anything has gone on Owen's record, because that is the one thing you will not do quietly. Answer that, and I'll take the rest upstairs.
